name: Nav2 (ROS 2 Navigation)
summary: The standard ROS 2 navigation stack: behavior-tree driven navigator, global planners (NavFn, Smac hybrid-A*/lattice, Theta*), local controllers (DWB, MPPI, Regulated Pure Pursuit), costmaps, recovery behaviors and waypoint following, including GPS waypoints via robot_localization.
why_it_matters: Default autonomy layer for ground robots in ROS 2; the place to plug a GNSS-denied localization source and still get full point-to-point and waypoint missions.
hackathon_notes: apt install ros-<distro>-navigation2 plus nav2_bringup gives a Gazebo TurtleBot demo in under an hour. Swap AMCL for your own localization by publishing map->odom TF. Tuning params YAML is the main time sink.

name: opennav_coverage
summary: Nav2-compatible complete-coverage task server and navigator built on Fields2Cover, with behavior-tree utilities for field/area coverage and row following.
why_it_matters: Gives Nav2 robots area-search and survey patterns (boustrophedon sweeps over a polygon) out of the box, useful for search, mapping and route clearance scenarios.
hackathon_notes: Needs a source build of Fields2Cover; send a polygon in GPS or map frame and get a coverage route. Best for flat open terrain.

name: OMPL - Open Motion Planning Library
summary: Library of sampling-based motion planners (RRT, RRT*, PRM, BIT*, informed variants, kinodynamic planners) with a clean state-space abstraction and Python bindings.
why_it_matters: The reference implementation for sampling-based planning; underpins MoveIt and many UAV/UGV planners, so it is the quickest way to get a correct baseline planner.
hackathon_notes: pip wheels exist for the Python bindings; define a state validity checker against your occupancy grid or DEM and you have a planner in an afternoon.

name: EGO-Planner
summary: ESDF-free gradient-based local planner for quadrotors from ZJU FAST Lab: optimizes B-spline trajectories using collision terms computed only where the trajectory hits obstacles.
why_it_matters: Lightweight onboard replanning for small drones flying through clutter; widely reused baseline for agile UAV navigation in unknown environments.
hackathon_notes: ROS1 (Noetic) with a bundled simulator; runs on a laptop. Porting to ROS 2 / PX4 needs a bridge. Good for a demo of reactive flight in a random forest map.

name: EGO-Swarm
summary: Decentralized multi-quadrotor extension of EGO-Planner with inter-agent collision avoidance and trajectory sharing over a network.
why_it_matters: Open reference for drone swarms that coordinate paths without a central server, relevant to contested comms scenarios.
hackathon_notes: Simulation launches many drones on one machine; trajectory broadcast assumes reliable comms - an interesting knob to degrade in a hackathon.

name: Fast-Planner
summary: HKUST quadrotor planning framework: kinodynamic A* front-end plus B-spline optimization, with topological and perception-aware variants for fast flight in unknown environments.
why_it_matters: Classic baseline that most later UAV planners compare against; modular enough to reuse its mapping (ESDF) and search components.
hackathon_notes: ROS1 + Gazebo-free lightweight sim; builds in minutes on Ubuntu 20.04. Expect NLopt dependency friction.

name: FUEL - Fast UAV Exploration
summary: Frontier-information-structure based autonomous exploration for quadrotors, combining global tour planning over frontiers with local viewpoint refinement.
why_it_matters: Autonomous mapping of unknown buildings or terrain without GNSS or prior map, a core reconnaissance capability.
hackathon_notes: Bundled sim; pairs naturally with a VIO/LiDAR odometry source from other lanes.

name: RACER - multi-UAV exploration
summary: Rapid collaborative exploration with multiple UAVs: decomposes unknown space and allocates exploration regions between drones with pairwise communication.
why_it_matters: A worked example of multi-robot task allocation for exploration under limited comms.
hackathon_notes: Same toolchain as FUEL; run 2-4 drones in sim and vary comm range.

name: GCOPTER
summary: General-purpose multicopter trajectory optimizer (MINCO) handling safe-corridor constraints and dynamic limits with spatial-temporal deformation.
why_it_matters: Efficient, well-documented trajectory optimizer to turn waypoint paths into flyable minimum-control trajectories.
hackathon_notes: Header-heavy C++ with ROS1 examples; best used as a library behind your own front-end.

name: GBPlanner
summary: NTNU ARL graph-based exploration planner for subterranean environments, used in the DARPA SubT challenge on legged and aerial robots.
why_it_matters: Exploration and return-home planning in GNSS-denied tunnels and caves, battle-tested in SubT.
hackathon_notes: ROS workspace with Gazebo SubT-like worlds; heavy but realistic.

name: CMU Autonomous Exploration Development Environment
summary: CMU ground-robot development environment with simulated worlds, terrain analysis, local planner and waypoint tools used for exploration research (TARE, FAR planner).
why_it_matters: Ready-made outdoor/indoor ground autonomy sandbox with terrain traversability built in.
hackathon_notes: Download the Unity/Gazebo environment and run; the local planner and terrain analysis nodes are reusable standalone.

name: KR Autonomous Flight
summary: UPenn Kumar Robotics end-to-end autonomy stack for GPS-denied quadrotors: state estimation, mapping, planning and control in one system.
why_it_matters: Full reference stack for flying without GNSS in forests and under canopy, from a lab with many field deployments.
hackathon_notes: Docker images help; large build. Use it to see how estimation and planning are glued, or reuse the planner.

name: MADER
summary: MIT ACL decentralized and asynchronous trajectory planner for multiple UAVs in dynamic environments with obstacle and agent avoidance.
why_it_matters: Multi-agent planning without synchronized clocks or central coordination, closer to real comms constraints.
hackathon_notes: No commits since 2022; ROS1. Use for ideas rather than code reuse.

name: Aerostack2
summary: ROS 2 framework for autonomous multi-aerial-robot systems: platform abstraction (PX4, DJI, Crazyflie, Gazebo), behaviors, mission scripting in Python and BT, and multi-drone coordination.
why_it_matters: One of the few ROS 2 native UAV mission frameworks that spans simulation to several real autopilots, good for multi-drone mission demos.
hackathon_notes: Binary packages for Humble; Python mission API lets you script takeoff/goto/land for several drones quickly.

name: PlanSys2
summary: PDDL-based symbolic planning system for ROS 2: domain/problem management, plan generation with off-the-shelf planners and execution via behavior trees.
why_it_matters: Turns high-level mission goals (visit, inspect, deliver) into executable action sequences, the missing layer above Nav2.
hackathon_notes: apt-installable; write a PDDL domain and wrap Nav2 goals as actions. Learning PDDL is the time cost.

name: BehaviorTree.CPP
summary: C++ behavior tree library with XML trees, async actions, logging and the Groot editor; the execution engine inside Nav2 and many mission frameworks.
why_it_matters: Standard way to compose navigation, fallback and recovery logic into readable mission trees.
hackathon_notes: Header-friendly library; Groot2 GUI helps demo mission logic to judges.

name: PythonRobotics
summary: Large collection of readable Python implementations of robotics algorithms: localization (EKF, particle filter), SLAM, path planning (A*, RRT*, D*, state lattice), path tracking and more, with animations.
why_it_matters: Best teaching and prototyping resource; copy a planner or filter into a hackathon prototype in minutes.
hackathon_notes: Pure numpy/matplotlib; no build. Good for a quick 2D planner over a rasterized DEM.

name: Fields2Cover
summary: Modular coverage path planning library: headland generation, swath generation, route ordering (boustrophedon, snake, spiral) and Dubins/Reeds-Shepp path smoothing, with Python bindings.
why_it_matters: Ready coverage planner for area search or survey patterns by ground or air vehicles.
hackathon_notes: Build from source with GDAL dependency; Python bindings let you produce a sweep over a GeoJSON polygon quickly.

name: polygon_coverage_planning
summary: ETH ASL coverage planner for polygons with holes that treats boustrophedon sweep selection as a generalized TSP, aimed at UAV survey.
why_it_matters: Handles no-fly holes inside a survey area, which simple lawnmower generators do not.
hackathon_notes: ROS1 + CGAL; last push 2023. Use as a reference or run offline to produce waypoint lists.

name: Elevation Mapping CuPy
summary: GPU elevation mapping from depth/LiDAR with traversability estimation and semantic layers, used on ANYmal legged robots.
why_it_matters: Terrain-aware planning for off-road robots needs a live elevation and traversability map; this is the modern GPU version.
hackathon_notes: Needs NVIDIA GPU and CuPy; Jetson supported. Outputs grid_map layers consumable by planners.

name: grid_map
summary: Universal multi-layer 2.5D grid map library for mobile robots with ROS/ROS 2 integration, filters, iterators and conversion to images, point clouds and costmaps.
why_it_matters: Common data structure for elevation, slope and cost layers - the glue between DEMs and planners.
hackathon_notes: Available as ROS 2 binaries; load a GeoTIFF DEM (via GDAL) into a grid_map layer for terrain-aware costs.

name: Spatio-Temporal Voxel Layer
summary: Nav2 costmap layer using OpenVDB voxel grids with time decay to represent 3D obstacles from depth and LiDAR sensors.
why_it_matters: Better 3D obstacle handling for ground robots in dynamic environments than the default voxel layer.
hackathon_notes: Drop-in Nav2 plugin via apt.

name: CBBA (Python)
summary: Python implementation of the Consensus-Based Bundle Algorithm for decentralized multi-agent task allocation with plotting examples.
why_it_matters: CBBA is the classic decentralized auction for assigning tasks to UAV teams; this is an easy-to-read starting point.
hackathon_notes: numpy + matplotlib only; wrap in a ROS 2 node or call from a mission script to assign search cells to drones.

name: Open-RMF rmf_task
summary: Task allocation library from Open-RMF that assigns tasks to fleets of robots, accounting for battery, travel time and task constraints.
why_it_matters: Production-grade multi-robot task allocation with a fleet-level view, transferable from logistics to multi-vehicle missions.
hackathon_notes: Part of the larger Open-RMF stack; worth it only if you want fleet management, otherwise use CBBA.

name: GDAL
summary: Translator library and CLI tools for raster and vector geospatial formats (GeoTIFF, COG, GeoPackage, Shapefile, KML and hundreds more) with reprojection, warping and DEM utilities.
why_it_matters: Every map, DEM and imagery pipeline goes through GDAL; gdalwarp, gdaldem and gdal_translate cover most reference-map preparation.
hackathon_notes: Use conda or the OSGeo Docker image to avoid version mismatches between GDAL and Python bindings.

name: PROJ
summary: Cartographic projection and coordinate transformation library with datum grids, time-dependent transformations and a pipeline syntax.
why_it_matters: Correct datum and projection handling (WGS84, ITRF, local grids, UTM) is foundational for any nav system that mixes map sources.
hackathon_notes: Bundle the proj-data grids offline if your demo has no internet.

name: pyproj
summary: Python interface to PROJ for CRS definitions, coordinate transformations and geodesic computations.
why_it_matters: Default Python tool for lat/lon <-> UTM/ECEF/local conversions in nav prototypes.
hackathon_notes: pip install pyproj ships PROJ inside the wheel; reuse a Transformer object for speed.

name: Rasterio
summary: Pythonic raster I/O on top of GDAL: read/write GeoTIFF and COG, windowed reads, masks and affine georeferencing.
why_it_matters: Easiest way to sample a DEM or orthophoto at a coordinate for terrain-referenced or visual navigation experiments.
hackathon_notes: pip wheels include GDAL; use windowed reads to crop tiles around a vehicle position.

name: QGIS
summary: Desktop open-source GIS for viewing, editing, analyzing and printing geospatial data, extensible via Python plugins.
why_it_matters: The analyst's workbench for building mission areas, inspecting DEMs and checking flight logs on a map.
hackathon_notes: Install the LTR build; draw AOIs and export GeoJSON for planners. QGIS loads MBTiles/PMTiles for offline basemaps.

name: CesiumJS
summary: WebGL 3D globe and map library with terrain, 3D Tiles, time-dynamic data (CZML) and accurate WGS84 rendering.
why_it_matters: Best open web option for a 3D situational awareness view with terrain and flight paths; widely used in defense demos.
hackathon_notes: npm install cesium. Default imagery/terrain use Cesium ion (token); for offline, serve your own quantized-mesh terrain and tiles.

name: Cesium Terrain Builder
summary: Command-line tools to convert GDAL-readable DEMs into Cesium terrain tiles (heightmap and quantized-mesh with the docker variant).
why_it_matters: Turns a Copernicus/SRTM DEM into offline 3D terrain for a CesiumJS display without internet.
hackathon_notes: Unmaintained since 2023; use the tum-gis docker image to avoid build pain.

name: MapLibre GL JS
summary: Open-source WebGL vector tile map renderer (fork of Mapbox GL JS v1) with styles, 3D terrain and globe view.
why_it_matters: Fast, license-clean 2D/2.5D web map for C2 dashboards, works fully offline with your own tiles.
hackathon_notes: Pair with martin or tileserver-gl and a PMTiles extract for an offline basemap.

name: OpenLayers
summary: Feature-rich web mapping library supporting many projections, WMS/WMTS, vector tiles and editing.
why_it_matters: Strong choice when you need non-Web-Mercator projections or OGC services in a C2 web UI.
hackathon_notes: npm install ol; integrates with proj4js for custom CRS.

name: Leaflet
summary: Small, simple JavaScript library for interactive raster/vector maps with a huge plugin ecosystem.
why_it_matters: Quickest route to a working map with markers and tracks in a hackathon UI.
hackathon_notes: Works with milsymbol to render unit icons as markers.

name: deck.gl
summary: GPU-powered large-scale data visualization framework with layers for points, paths, trips, hexbins and 3D tiles, usable over MapLibre or standalone.
why_it_matters: Renders thousands of tracks (ADS-B, AIS, swarm telemetry) smoothly for a common operating picture.
hackathon_notes: Use TripsLayer for animated track histories; integrates with React.

name: OSRM
summary: High-performance road routing engine on OpenStreetMap data using contraction hierarchies or multi-level Dijkstra.
why_it_matters: Offline road routing for ground vehicle convoy and logistics planning.
hackathon_notes: Docker image + a Geofabrik regional extract gives a routing API in under an hour.

name: Valhalla
summary: Tiled OSM routing engine with dynamic costing per request (auto, truck, pedestrian, bicycle), isochrones and map matching.
why_it_matters: Request-time costing makes it easy to avoid areas or prefer terrain types, and its map-matching snaps noisy tracks to roads.
hackathon_notes: Docker images available; build tiles for a region once and run offline. Elevation tiles enable grade-aware costing.

name: GraphHopper
summary: Java OSM routing engine usable as library or server, with custom models for per-request costing and map matching.
why_it_matters: Embeddable routing on JVM/Android, relevant for on-device dismounted navigation apps.
hackathon_notes: Single jar + OSM pbf; custom model JSON lets you penalize road classes or areas.

name: OSMnx
summary: Download, model and analyze street networks and other OSM features as NetworkX graphs.
why_it_matters: Rapid road/path graph construction for planners and task allocation experiments in Python.
hackathon_notes: pip install osmnx; needs internet for Overpass unless you load a local OSM file.

name: elevation
summary: CLI/Python tool to download, cache and clip global DEMs (SRTM, Copernicus DEM and others) for a bounding box.
why_it_matters: One-command DEM for an AOI, the first input for terrain-referenced navigation and terrain-aware planning.
hackathon_notes: Needs GDAL on PATH; eio clip --bounds ... produces a GeoTIFF.

name: TileServer GL
summary: Vector and raster tile server that serves MBTiles/PMTiles with GL styles and renders raster tiles server-side with MapLibre Native.
why_it_matters: Simplest offline basemap server for field laptops and TAK clients needing raster tiles.
hackathon_notes: docker run maptiler/tileserver-gl with an mbtiles file; also gives WMTS for QGIS.

name: Martin
summary: Fast Rust tile server for PostGIS, MBTiles and PMTiles sources, with tile generation and mbtiles tooling.
why_it_matters: Serves live PostGIS layers (tracks, zones) as vector tiles alongside static basemaps.
hackathon_notes: Single binary or docker; point at a PostGIS table to stream dynamic features.

name: PMTiles
summary: Single-file tile archive format and tooling, served by HTTP range requests from static storage, with JS/Go readers and extraction CLI.
why_it_matters: Ship an entire regional basemap as one file on a USB stick or static server - ideal for disconnected ops.
hackathon_notes: pmtiles extract from a planet build to cut your AOI; load with the MapLibre protocol plugin.

name: Planetiler
summary: Fast vector tile generator that builds OpenMapTiles-compatible tilesets from OSM extracts on a single machine.
why_it_matters: Build your own up-to-date offline basemap for an AOI in minutes.
hackathon_notes: java -jar planetiler.jar --area=<region> outputs mbtiles or pmtiles.

name: mgrs (Python)
summary: Python library converting between latitude/longitude and MGRS grid references, built on NGA GEOTRANS 3.10 (now a Rust port exposed through a pybind11 extension).
why_it_matters: MGRS is the grid language of military users; needed for any C2 UI or report generator.
hackathon_notes: pip install mgrs; mind the precision argument for 1 m vs 10 m references. Since 1.6.0 inverse conversion returns the grid-cell centre, not the south-west corner.

name: GeographicLib
summary: C++ library for accurate geodesic problems, UTM/UPS/MGRS conversions, geoid heights, gravity and magnetic field models.
why_it_matters: Gold-standard geodesy: geodesic distances, geoid (EGM96/2008) undulation for GNSS height vs DEM height, and MGRS.
hackathon_notes: Python and JS ports exist (geographiclib-python, geographiclib-js); geoid datasets download separately.

name: pymap3d
summary: Pure-Python 3D coordinate conversions: geodetic, ECEF, ENU, NED, AER, ECI, with optional NumPy vectorization.
why_it_matters: The everyday tool for converting GNSS fixes into a local ENU/NED frame for fusion and planning.
hackathon_notes: pip install pymap3d; no compiled deps.

name: sentinelhub-py
summary: Python client for Sentinel Hub and Copernicus Data Space services to search, download and process Sentinel and other satellite imagery.
why_it_matters: Pull recent satellite imagery of an AOI to build reference maps for visual geolocalization.
hackathon_notes: Needs free Copernicus Data Space or Sentinel Hub credentials; set up before the event.

name: pystac-client
summary: Python client for searching STAC APIs (Earth Search, Planetary Computer and others) by area, time and properties.
why_it_matters: Credential-free path to Sentinel-2, Landsat and Copernicus DEM tiles via public STAC catalogs.
hackathon_notes: Search Earth Search (AWS) without a key and read COGs directly with rasterio.

name: odc-stac
summary: Loads STAC items into xarray datasets with reprojection, resampling and mosaicking.
why_it_matters: Turn a STAC search into a ready, aligned raster stack for map-matching experiments.
hackathon_notes: Works with Dask for larger AOIs.

name: OpenDroneMap (ODM)
summary: Photogrammetry toolkit that turns aerial images into orthophotos, point clouds, 3D models and DEMs.
why_it_matters: Build your own up-to-date reference orthophoto and DSM from a survey flight for visual and terrain navigation.
hackathon_notes: docker run opendronemap/odm on a folder of images; WebODM gives a GUI. Processing time scales with image count.

name: TAK Server (open source)
summary: Open-source release of the TAK Server from the TAK Product Center: the federation and message routing server for ATAK/WinTAK/iTAK clients, handling CoT, data packages, missions and video.
why_it_matters: Reference C2 backend used by many government users; integrating with it makes a demo interoperable with fielded TAK clients.
hackathon_notes: Java + PostgreSQL + certificate setup is the main hurdle; use a docker recipe and allow several hours.

name: ATAK-CIV
summary: Source of the civilian Android Team Awareness Kit maintained by the TAK Product Center: map client, plugin SDK and CoT handling.
why_it_matters: The most widely used open tactical map client; plugins let you inject nav and sensor data into a fielded UI.
hackathon_notes: Building plugins needs the SDK and signing setup; for a hackathon, sending CoT to stock ATAK from the Play Store is far faster.

name: FreeTAKServer
summary: Python TAK-compatible situational awareness server supporting CoT routing, data packages, ExCheck and a REST API, with a web UI.
why_it_matters: Lightweight alternative to the official TAK Server for small exercises and demos.
hackathon_notes: pip/ZeroTouch installer; note no commits since late 2024, so check open issues before relying on it.

name: OpenTAKServer
summary: Actively developed open-source TAK server for ATAK, iTAK and WinTAK with web UI, video streaming integration, Meshtastic support and certificate enrollment.
why_it_matters: The easiest TAK backend to stand up in 2025-2026 with active maintenance.
hackathon_notes: Installer scripts for Ubuntu/RPi; get clients connected in about an hour.

name: GoATAK
summary: Go implementation of a simple ATAK-compatible server and a web client, supporting CoT over TCP/UDP/SSL.
why_it_matters: Single static binary TAK server and browser client - minimal footprint for edge devices.
hackathon_notes: go build or release binary; web map client is handy for judges without ATAK installed.

name: CloudTAK
summary: Browser-based TAK-compatible common operating picture with ETL connectors that push external data feeds into TAK.
why_it_matters: Shows how to bridge arbitrary data sources (sensors, APIs) into a TAK network with a web COP.
hackathon_notes: AWS-oriented deployment; locally, reuse its node-CoT library and connector patterns.

name: node-CoT
summary: JavaScript/TypeScript library for parsing, building and converting Cursor-on-Target messages, including GeoJSON conversion and TAK protobuf.
why_it_matters: Quickest way to emit CoT from a Node/web app.
hackathon_notes: npm install @tak-ps/node-cot.

name: PyTAK
summary: Python asyncio package for TAK integration: CoT send/receive over TCP, UDP, TLS and multicast, with helpers for building events.
why_it_matters: The go-to library for pushing vehicle positions, alerts or detections into ATAK from a Python nav stack.
hackathon_notes: pip install pytak; a 30-line script can stream a drone's estimated position to ATAK via multicast.

name: takproto
summary: Encode and decode TAK protobuf (TAK Protocol v1) packets, including mesh and stream formats.
why_it_matters: Needed when talking to modern TAK clients that prefer protobuf over XML CoT.
hackathon_notes: pip install takproto.

name: adsbcot
summary: Gateway that converts ADS-B data (dump1090/readsb JSON, ADSBExchange-style feeds) into CoT for display in TAK.
why_it_matters: Airspace awareness in TAK in minutes, useful context for UAV ops and C-UAS deconfliction.
hackathon_notes: Point at a local readsb aircraft.json and a TAK server URL.

name: cotlib (Go)
summary: Go library for parsing, validating and generating Cursor-on-Target XML with security-focused input limits and optional schema validation.
why_it_matters: Hardened CoT parsing for Go services that accept untrusted network input.
hackathon_notes: Schema validation needs libxml2 and CGO.

name: milsymbol
summary: Pure JavaScript library generating MIL-STD-2525 (B/C/D/E) and APP-6 (B/D/E) military symbols as SVG or canvas.
why_it_matters: Renders correct unit and track symbology on any web map without licensed assets.
hackathon_notes: npm install milsymbol; new ms.Symbol(sidc).asSVG() drops straight into a Leaflet or MapLibre marker.

name: Joint Military Symbology XML
summary: Esri data encapsulation of MIL-STD-2525D and APP-6(D) symbology: symbol IDs, entity tables and SVG assets.
why_it_matters: Machine-readable symbol tables useful for validating SIDCs or building your own renderer.
hackathon_notes: Archived in 2024; data still useful.

name: ASTERIX decoder (Croatia Control)
summary: C/C++ and Python decoder for EUROCONTROL ASTERIX surveillance data from files, stdin or network, with XML category definitions and JSON/XML output.
why_it_matters: ASTERIX is the format real radars and ATC surveillance use; decoding it lets a demo ingest professional air picture feeds.
hackathon_notes: Python module is on PyPI as asterix_decoder; feed it recorded or live UDP ASTERIX and get JSON per record.

name: asterix-specs
summary: EUROCONTROL ASTERIX category specifications in a structured machine-readable format, with generated JSON and docs.
why_it_matters: Authoritative-structured spec source for building ASTERIX encoders/decoders in any language.
hackathon_notes: Companion asterix-libs repo has generated Python libraries.

name: readsb
summary: ADS-B/Mode S decoder for RTL-SDR and other receivers with networking, JSON output, MLAT support and aggregation features.
why_it_matters: Cheap RTL-SDR plus readsb gives a live local air picture for airspace deconfliction.
hackathon_notes: Install via the wiedehopf script on Raspberry Pi; pairs with tar1090.

name: tar1090
summary: Improved web interface for readsb/dump1090 with track history, filtering and overlays.
why_it_matters: Instant browser air picture during a demo.
hackathon_notes: One install script; serves on the receiver.

name: pyModeS
summary: Python decoder for Mode S and ADS-B messages including Comm-B / EHS fields, with live streaming tools.
why_it_matters: Decode raw Mode S yourself, including derived wind and airspeed data; underlies The 1090MHz Riddle book.
hackathon_notes: pip install pyModeS; pairs with a Beast/raw feed from readsb.

name: traffic
summary: Toolbox for processing and analyzing air traffic trajectories: OpenSky access, filtering, resampling, airspace intersection and visualization.
why_it_matters: Analyze flight tracks and airspace structures for airspace awareness or UAV deconfliction studies.
hackathon_notes: pip install traffic; OpenSky historical data needs an account.

name: OpenSky API clients
summary: Python and Java bindings for the OpenSky Network REST API for live and recent aircraft states.
why_it_matters: Free crowd-sourced air picture when no local receiver is available.
hackathon_notes: Anonymous access is rate-limited. Since March 2026 authenticated access uses OAuth2 client credentials (basic auth was dropped); create an API client in your OpenSky account.
